Header:
Date: 2026-06-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SRE), Maya Chen (Fintera ML), Rajiv Kapoor (Fintera Platform), Elena Soto (Fintera PM), Tom Wu (Fintera Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy): Quick weekly poc sync focused on caching — prefix and KV cache hit rate discussion, observed drop during burst window, prompt reuse strategy, TTL tuning, next steps to share benchmarks and enable debug logging.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, this is our weekly caching sync — I'll just do a quick agenda: hit rates, recent run results, tuning ideas, and next steps.
[00:12] Maya: Thanks, Samir. Quick note, we saw hit rate drop last Wednesday during our 9am ET ramp. It fell from about 62% down to 18% for a ~20 minute window.
[00:22] Lena: mm-hmm, that matches what we saw on the Redwood side — looks like a lot of cold starts, prefix mismatch plus KV eviction activity.
[00:30] Rajiv: there's also a possibility of our routing change last week, we updated the upstream LB rules, could be related.
[00:36] Diego: (Redwood) I checked the logs, there were repeated small variations in the prompt templates causing prefix cache misses, and the KV cache got pressure because the sequence lengths spiked.
[00:48] Tom: from a security perspective we only saw normal auth spikes, no anomalies.
[00:52] [01:05] Samir: can you walk through the exact metrics you pulled, Lena? I want to make sure we're comparing apples to apples.
[01:12] Lena: sure, so our metric definitions: prefix hit rate = number of requests matched to an existing prefix entry / total requests. KV hit rate = successful KV cache lookups for given key during generation. We used 5-minute buckets; the spreadsheet I'll share uses the same windows. Note: some of the transcribed product names are funky in the logs, like "K-V cash" in one exported name, so watch the CSV mapping.
[01:35] Maya: yep saw that — our team also noticed slightly different tokenization when prompts included user metadata fields, like "acct_name" vs "account_name" — small text variation causing cache miss.
[01:48] Lena: Exactly — prompt reuse strategy idea: canonicalize user metadata fields in pre-processing, and use a short canonical prefix for the model call. That increased prefix hit rate in our internal test from 44% to 71%.
[02:06] Rajiv: how invasive is the canonicalization? Will that require changes in our front-end or can it be done in a middleware layer?
[02:12] Maya: we prefer not to touch front-end, middleware is fine. We have a gateway where we can add a small normalizer.
[02:18] Samir: that sounds good. For KV cache, one immediate knob is TTL and max-entries per shard. Lena, Diego — what do you recommend?
[02:26] Diego: For this workload, because you have many similar short sessions, increasing prefix TTL from 60s to 300s gave better amortization. For KV cache, bumping max-entries and switching eviction to LRU worked in our emulated test. Also consider pre-warming most frequent keys.
[02:41] Elena: when you say pre-warm, do you mean proactively insert keys from our top N templates?
[02:45] Lena: Yes, either via a warmup job or seeding during deploys. We can provide a warmup script.
[02:50] [03:00] Maya: we tried a warmup earlier but saw memory pressure — Rajiv, that's where our infra constraints hit.
[03:06] Rajiv: yeah we have memory caps per pod; raising them needs an infra change and procurement approval. We're planning a small increase but timing is rough.
[03:15] Samir: okay that's fair. Let's capture two parallel tracks: short-term (middleware canonicalization + TTL bump) and medium-term (increase memory, pre-warm, eviction policy change).
[03:26] [03:40] Lena: I also want to note that batching behavior affects KV usage: with larger continuous batching we see fewer per-token KV lookups because of shared KV cache references per batch; recommend increasing batch window slightly during non-latency-critical endpoints.
[03:56] Maya: latency is somewhat sensitive for our live agent product, but we have a background summarization job that's forgiving. We can apply aggressive batching there.
[04:05] Samir: good split. Now to concrete numbers — Samir shares recent benchmark: overall before fixes average prefix hit 59%, KV hit 52% across days; during the incident we saw prefix 18% and KV 12% at worst. After canonicalization test we ran, prefix went to ~70% and KV to ~63% in a 30-minute test. Spreadsheet link: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/fintera-caching-2026 (note: internal link, access controlled).
[04:35] Rajiv: can you export the CSV? Our side will import into Grafana.
[04:40] Samir: yes I'll share spreadsheet and a csv export.
[04:42] [05:00] Tom: security question: if we pre-warm keys, do we risk leaking PII into cache? We can't store customer PII in a shared cache.
[05:09] Lena: good point. Our recommendation: canonicalize and obfuscate PII before caching, or only cache non-PII-derived prefix keys. Also use per-tenant namespaces in the KV store — Redwood supports tenant-scoped keys.
[05:21] Maya: that's acceptable. We'll need a short security doc note for our compliance team.
[05:27] Samir: I'll attach the short security note and the SOC2/ISO page link.
[05:32] [06:00] Diego: one more thing — eviction pattern during the spike showed an uneven shard hot-spot. Looks like your traffic shape targeted a narrow key space for a short time which caused hot eviction. We can mitigate with hashing across shards or prefix sharding.
[06:14] Rajiv: we changed some routing rules last week that may have concentrated traffic. I'll re-check.
[06:18] Lena: In the meantime, we can tune the shard count and apply jitter to key assignment to spread load. We can also set a higher per-shard capacity in Dedicated mode if you go that route.
[06:31] [07:00] Elena: what's the Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoff here? Does Dedicated help with these cache pressure issues?
[07:07] Samir: Dedicated gives you reserved capacity, control over memory limits and shard sizing, and better isolation so you can bump cache sizes without noisy neighbors. Hosted can still work but you have to accept some limitations unless you move to a higher tier.
[07:21] Maya: At the moment we want to avoid Dedicated until we prove the canonicalization and TTL bump help. If they do, we'll look at Dedicated for Q3.
[07:28] [08:00] Lena: quick note on instrumentation — please enable these logs: prefix_match=true, kv_lookup=yes, kv_latency_ms, and include a request-id. That will help us pinpoint mismatches.
[08:12] Maya: we can enable those for a 48-hour window.
[08:15] Samir: perfect. Also we'll add a small helper script to compute hit-rate by canonicalized-prefix so you all see the delta.
[08:24] [09:00] Rajiv: any thoughts on prompt templating — we have many slightly different prompts which reduces reuse. Could Redwood do template normalization on our behalf?
[09:08] Lena: we can, but it requires a bit more integration. Short-term we recommend middleware normalization; medium-term Redwood can provide a small inline normalization layer as part of the request pipeline in Private deployments.
[09:21] Maya: also, are there known tokenization differences between our client and the model that cause split tokens and mismatches?
[09:28] Diego: small differences exist across tokenizers; we recommend using the same tokenizer step before cache-key construction. We'll share an example tokenizer snippet.
[09:35] [10:00] Samir: OK wrapping up with decisions: 1) Middleware canonicalization to standardize metadata keys, 2) Increase prefix TTL from 60->300s for non-sensitive endpoints, 3) Enable debug logs for 48h, 4) Lena to run load test with updated TTLs, 5) Rajiv to verify infra routing.
[10:17] Elena: agreed. Also request Samir to include security note re PII in cache.
[10:23] Samir: will do. I'll also add a short note on tenant-scoped keys and obfuscation.
[10:30] [11:00] Action recap (auto): Samir share spreadsheet + security note; Maya enable debug; Lena run load test; Rajiv confirm network.
[11:10] Samir: any other questions?
[11:13] Maya: nope all good, thanks.
[11:16] Rajiv: thanks all.
[11:20] [45:00] Meeting ends.
